title: GNoME predicts 2.2 million crystal structures, of which few may be useful new compounds
summary: Google DeepMind's GNoME proposed 2.2 million crystal structures (380,000 stable); independent reviews (Cheetham & Seshadri 2024, Kurlin 2026) find duplicates and scant evidence of useful compounds.
account: On 29 November 2023 Google DeepMind published GNoME in Nature. It reported 2.2 million structures below the convex hull, calling it “an order-of-magnitude expansion in stable materials known to humanity”. It stated that 736 of the stable structures had already been independently realized. The company blog adds that the Berkeley Lab A-Lab synthesized more than 41 materials from the predictions. Cheetham and Seshadri (UC Santa Barbara, Chem. Mater., 8 April 2024) examined the listings. They reported “scant evidence for compounds that fulfill the trifecta of novelty, credibility, and utility”. 404 Media (11 April 2024) quoted Cheetham that the paper “falls way short” as a practical contribution and DeepMind that it stands by all claims. C&EN (15 October 2026) reported an arXiv analysis by Vitaliy Kurlin (Liverpool). It found more than 15% near-duplicates within GNoME, about 24% duplicating Materials Project entries and about 17% close to ICSD entries. Leslie Schoop (Princeton) called some entries “completely unrealistic”. The Chem. Mater. critique itself was not available. Its abstract on Europe PMC (PMC11044265) is among the sources.
purpose: Predict stable inorganic crystal structures at scale to accelerate materials discovery
deployer: DeepMind (dataset released openly; stable structures contributed to the Materials Project)
taxonomy_note: Independent reviewers dispute the novelty and utility of the predicted structures.

ratings.reason: No individual beneficiary. A dataset release.
Use by the Materials Project and A-Lab is reported only by the vendor. Independent reviewers find scant utility.
No demonstrated downstream technology. Novelty of the predictions is disputed.

ai_role.statement: The graph-network model is the vendor's. Its predictions are documented in a vendor-authored Nature paper and blog. Independent reviewers (Cheetham & Seshadri 2024; Kurlin 2026 as reported by C&EN) report near-duplicates, unrealistic compounds and little evidence of useful novel materials. Benefit therefore rests on the vendor's account and is contested.

headline: GNoME's 2.2 million predicted crystals may include useful compounds

comparator.against: stable crystals previously identified by computational studies before GNoME
comparator.quote: Given that discovered materials compete for stability, the updated convex hull consists of 381,000 new entries for a total of 421,000 stable crystals, representing an-order-of-magnitude expansion from all previous discoveries.

later.note: Cheetham and Seshadri's April 2024 perspective in Chemistry of Materials examined the GNoME listings and found scant evidence of novel, credible and useful compounds, identifying every one of ten sampled 'stable structure' entries in the ICSD; C&EN reported further duplicate findings by Kurlin in October 2026.
later.quote: We examine the claims of this work here, unfortunately finding scant evidence for compounds that fulfill the trifecta of novelty, credibility, and utility.
